transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-09-02
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Location: Zoom / recording available
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Menon (Redwood SE), Alex Guerrero (Redwood CSM), Lina Ortiz (Quantiva CISO), Marco Hsu (Quantiva Platform), Priya Singh (Quantiva ML), Ethan Cole (Quantiva Legal)

[00:00:00] Jordan Lee: Hey everyone thanks for joining, we wanted to keep this focused on the security checklist items you flagged in last week's intake. Quick round robin intros if anyone new?
[00:00:12] Lina Ortiz: Lina, CISO at Quantiva. We're just trying to close the pilot compliance gates so we can get budget signoff.
[00:00:18] Marco Hsu: Marco, infra lead. I'm mainly concerned about SSO and audit logs streaming.
[00:00:22] Priya Menon: Priya here from Redwood, I'll drive the SAML/SCIM and logging pieces on our side.
[00:00:30] Jordan Lee: Great. Quick agenda: SOC2 artifacts, SSO integration status, audit logging & retention options, data retention and redaction, and then confirm next steps.

[00:02:15] Marco: We tried the quick Okta link you sent, got a 403 on the metadata endpoint. I think staging IPs arent whitelisted?
[00:02:30] Priya Menon: Ah yes, for the pilot staging we spin up ephemeral endpoints, we should have given you the IP range. Sorry, Jordan can you paste the staging IP block in the chat?
[00:02:40] Jordan Lee: Sure, sending now. Also note we support SP-initiated and IdP-initiated flows, Okta works fine. We also support SCIM for provisioning, if you want us to do automated user sync.
[00:03:05] Marco: SCIM would be ideal. How granular are roles via SCIM? We need at least read-only ops and admin roles.
[00:03:18] Priya Menon: You can map SCIM groups to Redwood RBAC roles; common pattern is to have pilot-admin and pilot-user groups. We also support group attribute mapping. Not all attributes are required, but we can supply a template.

[00:05:45] Lina: On audit logs, what fields are included by default? We need user id, request path, model id, token counts, response latency, and IP. Also must show policy decisions for fallback routing.
[00:06:05] Priya Menon: Default audit log includes request metadata: timestamp, user id, route, model version, token usage, latency and outcome status. IP is included but masked by default if you enable PII minimization. We can toggle redaction at the workspace level.
[00:06:27] Marco: Masked IP is okay if we can ship full logs to our Splunk bucket when needed.
[00:06:35] Alex Guerrero: For the pilot we recommended exporting raw audits to a customer-owned S3 bucket in the same region, and we can write to S3 or directly to Splunk HEC. That avoids storing long-term on Redwood side.

[00:08:50] Priya Singh: Just to clarify, how long does Redwood keep logs by default? Our legal wants 7 years for eDiscovery, but we obviously can't keep identifiable PII forever.
[00:09:05] Priya Menon: Default retention on hosted is 90 days for full logs and 365 days for aggregated metrics. For enterprise/private we can configure retention and archiving policies — e.g., ship to your S3 for long-term retention and we can purge from our side after X days.
[00:09:20] Ethan Cole: From legal: we need the export to include a tamper-evident manifest or checksum, for chain-of-custody. Is that supported?
[00:09:31] Jordan Lee: We can include SHA256 checksums per file upload and a signed manifest for each archive. We do that as part of our compliance export feature. I'll include docs.

[00:12:00] Marco: For the SSO flow test, can we do a live test in this call? I can share my Okta staging screen.
[00:12:10] Jordan Lee: Good idea, but maybe let's not debug live now; instead Priya will send a test plan and a short checklist, then we schedule a 30-min SAML test with your IdP.
[00:12:22] Priya Menon: I'll put together the test plan: SP metadata, required claims, cert rotation guidance, and a SCIM provisioning test script. That will include expected audit entries per step.

[00:15:40] Lina: SOC2 — you said you'd share the Type II report and the in-scope system boundary. Can we get the last 12 months' SOC2 and pen test?
[00:15:52] Jordan Lee: Yes. We have our SOC2 Type II 2024 report (redacted), recent pen test executive summary and a compliance mapping doc that maps controls to features. I'll send this by EOD Friday.
[00:16:08] Ethan Cole: Will these artifacts be blotted with vendor redaction? Our procurement team needs to see scope and any subservice organizations.
[00:16:17] Jordan Lee: We'll provide a vendor-appropriate redaction and include a list of subprocessors and hosting providers. We'll also provide the control mapping sheet.

[00:20:05] Marco: On encryption, does Redwood support customer-managed keys? We have to use our KMS for ePHI in pilot if possible.
[00:20:18] Priya Menon: For Private deployments yes, you can bring your own KMS or HSM. For dedicated hosted we have workarounds — envelope encryption with a customer-wrapped key is supported in dedicated tiers. For hosted multi-tenant, we currently use provider-managed keys, but we can arrange dedicated encryption for enterprise contracts.
[00:20:40] Lina: For the pilot we need to keep ePHI in our VPC and ensure logs only go to our S3. Can the pilot be run in a VPC-private mode?
[00:20:50] Alex Guerrero: We can run a private pilot using our Redwood Private agent in your VPC. That was part of the Dedicated offering discussion; for the pilot we can deploy a constrained private stack in your cloud account with limited ingress. We'll need an infra engagement.
[00:21:05] Marco: How long to stand that up?
[00:21:09] Priya Menon: Typical pilot private deployment is 7-10 business days for staging with our infra team if credentials and network peering info are available.

[00:25:30] Marco: Audit log schema — can we add a custom field for internal customer-owner tag? We want to map requests back to our internal user id.
[00:25:40] Priya Menon: Yes, we support a request metadata header you can set from your app (x-quantiva-user-id) and it will surface in the audit log. Just be mindful of PII policies if that header contains ePHI.
[00:25:55] Marco: We'll hash the identifier before sending.

[00:28:10] Lina: About access controls — we need SSO + SSO SCIM provisioning + 2FA enforcement and admin approval flows. Can Redwood enforce 2FA for all logins?
[00:28:25] Priya Menon: If you federate via SAML and your IdP enforces 2FA, then Redwood respects that. For non-federated users we can require TOTP but it's unusual for enterprise SSO flow.

[00:31:12] Jordan Lee: A question from our side: for the pilot success criteria you had listed 'no P0 security issues, logs ingested to Splunk within 10 minutes, and SAML integration completed' — is that still the bar for the week?
[00:31:28] Lina Ortiz: Yes, roughly. Also legal wants the evidence that audit logs contain request granularity we discussed, plus a signed export capability.

[00:34:00] Priya Menon: On retention policy we propose: pilot default local retention 14 days, auto-ship to your S3 nightly and retention there controlled by you. We can purge after configured days. For long-term legal retention, we recommend archival to Glacier with a checksum manifest.
[00:34:20] Ethan Cole: That works. Please include the manifest format in the doc.

[00:38:55] Marco: About the audit log test: what format will the logs be in? JSON lines? Parquet?
[00:39:05] Alex Guerrero: We support JSON lines (NDJSON) for immediate ingestion and Parquet for bulk archival. Splunk HEC ingestion expects JSON so NDJSON is easiest for the test.
[00:39:18] Marco: Ok NDJSON is fine.

[00:43:10] Priya Singh: Quick ML question: if we enable prefix caching and KV cache, are those entries going to show up in logs or are they internal only? We need to prove cache hits for cost audit.
[00:43:25] Priya Menon: We emit cache hit metrics in aggregated metrics and we also include cache event logs (hit/miss) as part of the audit stream when enabled. Those can be redacted if needed.

[00:46:40] Lina: Anything else on legal/compliance?
[00:46:45] Ethan Cole: Just procurement asks: we will need a data processing addendum and a statement of work for the pilot with SLAs and exit criteria. Can you produce a draft?
[00:46:55] Jordan Lee: Yes, I'll draft a DPA and SOW template and share with Ethan. We'll keep the pilot SLOs minimal but measurable.

[00:49:50] Priya Menon: To recap action items: I'll send SAML/SCIM test plan, we'll enable audit logs to your S3 for the test, Jordan will send SOC2 artifacts and pen test summary, Alex will create the pilot workspace and open the Jira, Marco will provide Okta metadata and test creds.
[00:50:20] Marco: Sounds good. One more: can we get an optional guide for log redaction rules so our compliance team can set policies?
[00:50:28] Priya Menon: Yes we have a redaction policy doc and sample regexes; I'll include that.

[00:51:30] Jordan Lee: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up via email and get the SAML deep-dive scheduled.
[00:51:37] Lina Ortiz: Thanks, bye.
[00:51:40] Meeting end.
